CVE-2026-125336.title: Forge: X.509 nameConstraints not enforced by verifyCertificateChain()
CVE-2026-125336.description: Forge (also called node-forge) is a native implementation of Transport Layer Security in JavaScript. Prior to 1.4.3, pki.verifyCertificateChain() in lib/x509.js does not decode or enforce the X.509 nameConstraints extension while validating certificate paths. A name-constrained certificate authority with a non-critical extension can therefore issue a leaf certificate with a subjectAltName dNSName or subject commonName outside a permitted subtree or inside an excluded subtree, and node-forge accepts the chain. Exploitation requires a name-constrained CA that chains to a trusted root and either its private key or the ability to obtain an out-of-scope certificate, allowing impersonation of names outside the delegated namespace, including against forge.tls clients. Chains without nameConstraints are not affected, and affected versions safely reject critical nameConstraints as unsupported rather than accepting them. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.3.

CVE-2026-99565.title: ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU
CVE-2026-99565.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU

The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before
the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU
can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined
SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter
SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer.

An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE
that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection
is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU.
This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without
changing when need_neg is cleared.

CVE-2026-99749.title: ksmbd: enforce the read-only share flag when creating a stream
CVE-2026-99749.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: enforce the read-only share flag when creating a stream

When a share is read-only, smb2_open() rejects opens that would create
or truncate a file. Creating a named stream on an existing file with
streams_xattr sets neither O_CREAT nor O_TRUNC, so it passes this check,
and smb2_set_stream_name_xattr() then creates the stream. On a Time
Machine share, opening a missing AFP_AfpInfo stream also writes one. A
user who can write a file at the filesystem level can therefore add
streams to it through a read-only share.

Do not create a stream or synthesize AFP_AfpInfo when the share is not
writable. Existing streams still open normally, and a missing stream
opened with FILE_OPEN still returns STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_NOT_FOUND.
